request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now carry a to-date. All 4 acceptance tests pass in `bin/e2e`.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V31__rate_to.sql`, adds a `to_date` column to rates. The database also refuses a to-date before the from-date.
- **Server:**
  - The rate form and the rate shown on screen both carry `to`.
  - Setting a rate refuses a to-date before its from-date with a 400 and writes nothing.
  - Setting a rate for an existing grade and from-date replaces its to-date too: leaving it empty removes any end date.
  - `RATE_SET` adds ` to=<date>` at the end of the line when one was given.
- **Which rate applies:** a claim still gets the latest rate whose from-date is on or before its date. If that rate's to-date is before the claim's date, the claim has no rate and its due is n/a. That one change in `RateRepository.findInForce` carries through to everything that reads due: person and sheet totals skip the claim, a statement binds it at n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to, and the rollup audit lines follow.
- **Front end:** the rates form has a To field (`rate-form-to`) and the rate list shows it (`rate-to`). `rateOn` applies the same end-date rule, so the screen's dues and each grade's "current rate" show n/a once the rate in force has ended.

**One behaviour you might not expect:** when the form refuses a to-date because it's before the from-date, it also clears the To field. The error message says so. I added this because the first test failed without it: the refused to-date stayed in the form, and the next rate the test set (from-date only) picked it up and was wrongly refused too.
